title: I built a 3D ski resort tycoon game with Claude Code. Free in the browser
author: phildbs
selftext:
I've been building Mountain Mogul, a ski resort tycoon game you play in the browser: https://mtmogul.com (free, no download, works on phones).

You start with an untouched, forested mountain. You cut trails, build chairlifts and lodges, make snow, set ticket prices and try not to go bankrupt before the snow shows up. Every guest is simulated: they park, rent skis, pick runs that suit their ability, queue for lifts and go home when their legs give out.

HOW IT WAS MADE

The code was written by Claude (Claude Code), working in my GitHub repo. My job was more like a producer or play-tester:

• I describe a feature or a bug, often with a phone screenshot ("this parking lot looks like it's floating").

• Claude builds it, runs automated tests, and sends me screenshots, including phone-sized ones.

• I play it, give feedback, and say "publish" when I'm happy. It deploys to GitHub Pages.

WHAT'S UNDER THE HOOD

• A single HTML file (about 11,700 lines) using three.js for the 3D mountain, with terrain generation, terrain grading, creek bridges, chairlift towers and an agent-based guest simulation.

• Supabase for sign-in, cloud saves, leaderboards, likes, creator profiles and crash reports.

• 41 automated test scenarios run in a headless browser (Playwright) before each release.

WHAT WORKED WELL

• Screenshot-driven feedback. "This looks wrong" plus a picture was usually enough.

• Making it write tests for everything. That's what lets it change one part without quietly breaking another.

• Asking it to look at real player data before adding features. Most new resorts were stalling in pre-season, which led to an in-game advisor that explains what to do next.

WHAT WAS HARDER

• Visual polish takes several rounds. Creek bridges took a few tries before they stopped looking like they were sinking into the banks.

• A big single-file codebase means you have to be specific about what you want changed.

Would love feedback, especially from anyone who's played tycoon games. What would make you keep playing?
